name: Brouc
description: Le Brouc is a Swiss four-player point-trick partnership game of the marriage group, played with a 32-card French-suited pack and scoring for card points and marriages (including extended K-Q-J combinations).
deck: 32 cards (Standard 32: A, 10, K, Q, J, 9, 8, 7 in each suit)

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: Switzerland (l’Etivaz, canton of Vaud)
Time Period: Early 1800s (first known description 1802)
Historical Development: Local point-trick game in the marriage group, related to other Swiss ace-ten games and described in French-language club rules.
Cultural Significance: Traditional partnership game of l’Etivaz with organised local and championship play.
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

scoring.description: Teams accumulate card points and marriage bonuses across deals; scores are rounded to the nearest 10, written on a slate, and compared to a target threshold.
scoring.winCondition: The partnership whose cumulative score (rounded slate total plus current hand) first reaches at least 301 points (30 and 1) wins the game; matches can also be scored by coches in tournament play.
